ma_whipple_boulder.blurb: A single boulder on the hillside just beyond the top of Whipple Hill, in a small conservation area on the Lexington side of the Boston suburbs. It holds ten problems, mostly easy and moderate: a solid core around V0 to V2, then one V3, one V5 and a lone V7 for the strong. Holds are plentiful, landings are good, and the faces look away from the trail, with east and south sides photographed. It suits a short, relaxed session for newer boulderers; the rest of the hill is not a destination for climbing, so plan this as a quick stop rather than a day out.

ma_deer_hill_boulder.blurb: One lone block, roughly ten to twelve feet tall, sitting on the edge of Spot Pond in the Middlesex Fells north of Boston. It is tucked away from the busier parts of the Fells and has a quiet, out-of-the-way feel. All ten problems are sit starts and sit very close together in difficulty: eight around V1 and two at V2, so there is nothing hard here. The rock is solid and the lines are good, which makes it a pleasant place for a warm-up or a solo evening with a single pad.

ma_chunk_the.blurb: A compact boulder about nine feet tall in Douglas State Forest, central Massachusetts, set a short way beyond the Squirrel Cave face in the Mine Brook boulder group. Ten problems cover a wide spread: a few V0 to V2 warm-ups, a middle band around V3 to V5, and several hard lines up to V7. Granite here tends to be featureless, so expect slopers and small crimps. East and south faces have been photographed. Local climbers rate it among the best climbing in the state forest, and more lines are said to remain unclimbed.
ma_chunk_the.approach: Follow the trail to the Mine Brook boulder group, roughly 0.9 miles with little elevation change. The Chunk sits to the right, about twenty meters past the Squirrel Cave face.

ma_approach_boulder_the.blurb: A clean, well-worn block that sits right on the main trail leading up into the Redrocks climbing area on Cape Ann, close to the Pink Floyd, Main and Masters walls. Ten problems run from moderate to very hard: about half sit at V3 to V5, a few are V6 to V7, and one outlier is far harder. The most popular lines are mid-grade V3 problems. The boulder stands within about a hundred feet of the highway, so passing traffic is loud. Cape Ann stone is granite, and it works well as a first stop on a Redrocks visit.
